A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAIA work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting comparison. All supplied pages were inspected, including v1 Appendices A–E. v2 contains no appended supplementary material, despite referring readers to it; judgments concern the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original GUI planning and grounding experiments, critic comparisons, rollout ablations and qualitative examples in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and additionally reports latency measurements and an analysis of 300 negative training examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the two-round action-data flywheel, binary ICM training with cross-entropy, best-of-N selection and ICM-r2 refinement. The added action-labeling descriptions do not establish a change to the algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Both versions use AndroidControl and GUI-Odyssey for training and planning evaluation, and ScreenSpotV2 for grounding evaluation. AndroidControl high- and low-level settings and ScreenSpotV2 mobile, desktop and web coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding planning and grounding tables retain the same baseline and guided-agent membership. The comparisons against UI-Genie-RM and the GRPO-trained Reasoning Critic Model also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds latency measurements at N=1, 2, 4 and 8 using vLLM actor inference and parallel critic scoring, plus a composition analysis sampling 300 negatives. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. Newly stated action-matching rules document labeling details rather than demonstrate a revised protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds computation-cost analysis and an action-type breakdown of sampled negatives. Existing rollout and critic-type ablations remain. v1 Figures 5 and 7 reappear as v2 Figures 5 and 6; the other two appendix examples are absent from the supplied v2, rather than replaced by new cases.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The retained N-rollout experiments concern candidate sampling, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Benchmark accuracy values remain unchanged, but UI-TARS 1.5 plus ICM-r2 AndroidControl-High improvement annotations change from 4.5/3.8/7.4 to 4.4/6.6/9.8 for Type/GR/SR in v2 Table 2. New Table 5 reports total latency rising from 1.4882 seconds at N=1 to 3.2514 at N=8. Section 4.1 newly reports Click/Open/Swipe/Type shares of 64%/13%/9%/4% among 300 negatives.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, policy and critic definitions, cross-entropy objective, selection rule and flywheel dataset definitions are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: realistic action-data curation, iterative intuitive-critic improvement and test-time gains across open- and closed-source GUI agents. The shortened conclusion preserves these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 newly qualifies the retained temperature-conversion example: clicking a Back icon and issuing system Back can be semantically equivalent despite different benchmark labels. Section 4.4 adds interpretations about practical overhead and parallel execution, including an actor-dominance claim that conflicts with Table 5 at N=8.

D1.justification: v1 Appendices B–D provide model-specific prompts, marked-image inputs, LoRA and optimizer settings, batch size, epochs and selection code; these are absent from the supplied v2, which redirects readers to supplementary material. v2 adds the 14% click-label threshold, other matching rules, inference infrastructure details and a repository location for a promised code/data/datasheet release. This substantially changes accessible documentation without establishing changed training settings.

R1.justification: The supplied v2 drops the FlashAttention, LoRA and Set-of-Mark references associated with v1's appendix. Main related-work positioning remains intact; several other references merely receive publication or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Although much main-text prose is retained, document structure changes substantially: v2 adds Computation Efficiency and Case Study subsections, integrates selected appendix cases, and omits the standalone ethics, reproducibility and appendix sections. It also revises the evaluation explanation and condenses the conclusion.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different page template, typography and running headers, splits v1 Table 1 into Tables 2–3, relocates the data-distribution table and adds a latency table. Selected appendix figures move into the main text, while prompt/code displays and two case figures are absent. Shared pipeline diagrams and rollout plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful labeling details, latency evidence, corrected improvement annotations and an equivalent-action caveat. However, the supplied paper loses the prompts, training parameters and implementation code available in v1, weakening reproducibility; references to an unsupplied supplement do not restore that information. Its new efficiency interpretation also contradicts Table 5: at N=8, critic latency is 1.9897 seconds versus 1.2617 for the actor. These losses outweigh the limited additions, while the central method and benchmark evidence remain intact.
